_comment: Skills whose trigger-probe status (`never` / `STALE`) is KNOWN and ACCEPTED, read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/case_coverage.py's P004. Probing costs live model calls (~$0.05/probe, $6.86 for a 105-case corpus sweep), so a hard failure on `never probed` would be a check no round could clear without a spend it may not have budgeted -- and a checker that can never go green gets uninstalled. An entry silences P004 for that skill. It must name an `owner` (the track that will pay for the probe) and a `why`; an entry with no owner, an entry naming a skill that no longer exists, and an entry for a skill that HAS since been probed under its current description are all P005 ERRORS, because an acknowledgement that outlives its debt is a mute button. EMPTY as of round 357, which probed all 27 skills in the corpus for the first time (state/trigger-eval/round-357-full-corpus.{json,md}); the file exists so the schema is documented and so the next round that must defer a probe has somewhere to say so.

losses-name-their-winner.why: New in round 405 (skills B) -- authored by the round that PAID this file's seven-round batch, and deliberately not probed by it. Two reasons, both recorded rather than assumed. (1) The batch had already spent 205 probes / $11.97 and a round that probes its own new paraphrase scores its own wording (round 357 item 3's independence concern, the same reason round 373 registered rather than probed). (2) More usefully: this skill's own subject says the confusable you NAME is not the one that wins, so naming its nearest sibling here would be the exact error it documents. What it does instead is name the MEASURABLE prediction -- run `displacement.py claims --only <the probing round's runs>` afterwards and see which skill actually takes lntw-near/mid/far. Its negative case lntw-neg-replicate deliberately expects repeats-are-not-replicates, which is the one genuine boundary (that skill answers 'did the loss replicate', this one answers 'who won'); repeats-are-not-replicates had a BODY-ONLY upgrade this round, so its digest ebd7016b65db is unchanged and round 393's probe of it still applies. Probe at >=4 separate invocations at --repeats 1 plus ONE at --repeats 2 (round 405's design, section 2 of its knowledge file), not at round 393's 3 x --repeats 2 -- and re-derive rho first, because round 405 measured 0.143 where round 393 measured 0.333.

cause-needs-a-denominator.why: New in round 406 (NUC-integration E), registered unprobed under the standing convention rounds 373/375/377/378/379/394/395/398/401/402 all used: a probe is a priced run and belongs to a skills(B) batch, and a round probing its own paraphrase scores its own wording. This entry deliberately does NOT name a confusable to probe against, which is a change from every prior entry in this file and is round 405's measured finding applied rather than quoted: of the five skills whose description named a sibling AND lost a probe, ZERO had that named sibling as their top measured taker, and 49% of losses were abstentions no pair rewrite can reach. Naming one here by reading would be guessing. What to do instead: probe cnd-near/mid/far, then run `displacement.py claims --only <that round's runs>` and let the measurement name the taker. The prediction on record is that cnd-far ('the same job shows up in every incident window') is the weakest of the three, because its surface reads as pattern-finding rather than attribution and the skill's own subject is why that reading is wrong. The negative case cnd-neg-mechanism expects NO skill: a bisect that reproduces is a mechanism, and the SKILL.md says explicitly that a mechanism outranks the counting -- a description that fires on it is too broad. Re-derive rho before sizing the batch; round 405 measured 0.143 on 18 cases against round 393's 0.333 on 7.

verdict-carries-its-threshold.why: New in round 407 (SWE-loop D), registered unprobed by the track that wrote it rather than probed by it -- the standing reason (round 373, round 405 item 1): a round that probes its own fresh paraphrase scores its own wording. What round 405 asked for INSTEAD of a named rival is recorded here as a measurable prediction, so `displacement.py claims` can score it: I predict vct-near/mid/far lose most often to ABSTENTION rather than to any sibling, because this description names a shape (a boolean compared across runs) and not a domain, and round 405 measured 49% of losses in its own designed runs as abstentions. If a taker does appear I predict `carried-claim-rot` on vct-far (the lint case reads like a stale-number case) and `pristine-checkout-differential` on vct-mid; both of those are guesses by READING, which is exactly what round 405 showed to be wrong 5 times out of 5, so score them as predictions and not as boundaries to rewrite toward. Probe at >=4 separate invocations at --repeats 1 plus ONE at --repeats 2 (round 405's design), and re-derive rho first rather than quoting 0.143 or 0.333.
